relevance_note: Case report of one Japanese man with LCAT deficiency: 'We identified a homozygous C to T point mutation at nucleotide 501 (g.501 C＞T) of exon 4 at codon 140'; two previously reported carriers (refs 12 and 13) are also described by variant.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON and checked every span verbatim. Table 1 has the single patient as the value column (header row 'a measurement | | (normal range)'). Contradiction/oddity: the paper writes the protein change as 'A140C' and 'A140H' while the text says arginine (Arg) to cysteine (Cys) and Arg to His; recorded the strings as printed (one-letter 'A' conflicts with Arg). The paper labels the nucleotide change 'g.501C＞T' (with a full-width '＞'; abstract writes 'g.501 C＞T' with a space); no c. or transcript is printed, so cdna is null and the g. string is copied to genomic_coordinates_as_stated as printed. Variant type 'missense' rests on 'amino acid substitution' wording. Two previously published people are included because the paper gives their variant: 'ref 12) patient' (Japan, congress proceeding, same mutation, stated unrelated) and 'ref 13) patient' (Austria, A140H; the gene symbol span for this row comes from reference 13's title). Their zygosity and features are not given. Age at diagnosis left not reported: the paper gives age 57 at presentation/report but no explicit age at diagnosis. Hypertriglyceridemia rests only on Table 1 (173 mg/dL vs range 30-149); the text does not call it high. 'Chest radiography, electrocardiography, and echocardiography gave essentially normal findings' is recorded as written and excludes nothing more specific (atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease left not reported). Renal function was normal at presentation (UN, Cre within normal limits) but 'gradually declined' later under ARB treatment; chronic kidney disease left not reported as not explicitly stated. Mesangial deposits are described as 'high-density deposits' and vacuoles, not as lipid or expansion, so that checklist item is not reported; 'few tubulo-interstitial changes' does not explicitly name atrophy or fibrosis, so not reported. Family history unclear (parents divorced); no parental testing; consanguinity not reported.
